tldr_label: TL;DR: The Kremlin confirms a Trump-Xi-Putin meeting, Iran strikes at Bahrain again, and the Houthis take the Bab el-Mandeb coast

tldr_bullets.label: APEC
tldr_bullets.body: The Kremlin confirmed that Putin, Xi and Trump will meet in Shenzhen on November 19. Beijing has not confirmed, and Ukraine is not on the White House agenda. [[TAG:info:Nov 19]]

tldr_bullets.label: Gulf
tldr_bullets.body: Bahrain said it intercepted a second round of Iranian drone attacks in three days. Iran's navy claims mines set three tankers ablaze near Hormuz, which the US has not confirmed. [[TAG:danger:escalation]]

tldr_bullets.label: Red Sea
tldr_bullets.body: Yemeni government-aligned forces withdrew from the area overlooking the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, leaving the Houthis in control. [[TAG:danger:second chokepoint]]

tldr_bullets.label: Alliances
tldr_bullets.body: Turkey and Qatar signed a mutual defence pact, and the Philippines and Australia upgraded their defense arrangement. [[TAG:info:new pacts]]

tldr_bullets.label: US
tldr_bullets.body: A router fault triggered a nationwide FAA ground stop, only the third in US history. Treasury Secretary Bessent confirmed he moved to a military base after Iranian threats. [[TAG:warning:systems strained]]

sections.title: Shenzhen Summit Confirmed
sections.summary: Kremlin says the Putin-Xi-Trump meeting is set for Nov 19; China silent; Ukraine off the agenda

paragraphs.heading: Moscow Confirms
paragraphs.body: Anadolu and Al Arabiya reported that Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said on Saturday that Putin, Xi and Trump will hold a trilateral meeting in Shenzhen on November 19, alongside the APEC summit. He called it 'extremely significant' but said any agreements could not be imposed on other nations. China has not yet confirmed the meeting. [[TAG:info:Beijing silent]]

paragraphs.heading: Agenda
paragraphs.body: According to the reports, the White House said the talks would cover global nuclear arms reduction and the Middle East war, but not Ukraine. Al Jazeera and CBS News described it as the first meeting of its kind. A digest on No1's Daily Digest noted that the format leaves Kyiv out. [[TAG:warning:Kyiv excluded]]

sections.title: Gulf and Red Sea: Pressure on the Straits
sections.summary: Bahrain intercepts Iranian drones; Iran claims mined tankers; Houthis gain Bab el-Mandeb coast

paragraphs.heading: Bahrain Again
paragraphs.body: France 24 and Dawn reported that Iran launched its second drone attack on Bahrain in three days. Bahrain's Defense Force said the drones were intercepted before reaching their targets. Kurdistan24 reported that the Revolutionary Guards claimed six drones hit a US air-defense radar at the Riffa base, without offering evidence. Bloomberg reported that Iran repeated that a path to a deal with the US remains open. [[TAG:danger:second strike in 3 days]]

paragraphs.heading: Mined Tankers
paragraphs.body: Anadolu and ANI reported that Iran's navy said tankers caught fire after hitting naval mines near the Strait of Hormuz. Accounts range from two to three ships. Iran said the vessels were using an unauthorized route with their tracking systems off. It did not name the ships or report casualties, and there was no independent confirmation. The US military says it has cleared the strait's routes of mines. [[TAG:warning:unconfirmed]]

paragraphs.heading: Bab el-Mandeb
paragraphs.body: Al-Monitor and The National reported that southern Yemeni forces aligned with the government withdrew from the Dhubab area overlooking the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, leaving the Houthis in control. The forces called it a redeployment to secure Aden. Daily Sabah reported that Saudi Arabia struck Houthi targets in response. [[TAG:danger:Red Sea risk]]

paragraphs.heading: Turkey-Qatar Pact
paragraphs.body: Al Jazeera and France 24 reported that Turkey and Qatar signed a mutual defence agreement in Istanbul, pledging a unified stance against any external armed attack on either country. Turkey said the pact is not aimed at any other country and is open to others, including Egypt. [[TAG:info:mutual defence]]

sections.title: United States
sections.summary: Router fault grounds all US flights for hours; Bessent confirms move to base over Iran threats

paragraphs.heading: Ground Stop
paragraphs.body: Al Jazeera and CNN reported that the FAA halted flights nationwide on Friday afternoon after a telecommunications outage hit all 22 air route traffic control centers. The ground stop was lifted that night. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy blamed overloaded routers in an aging system. The root cause was still under investigation as of Saturday. Reports said it was only the third nationwide ground stop in US history. [[TAG:warning:aging system]]

paragraphs.heading: Bessent
paragraphs.body: CBS News and The Hill reported that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent confirmed he moved from his Washington home to a military base at the Secret Service's direction after Iranian threats against his life. He said he would not be cowed. The Hill reported that Hegseth and Rubio are also living on military bases. Iran has previously denied plotting attacks on US soil. [[TAG:danger:threats to officials]]

paragraphs.heading: Iran Policy
paragraphs.body: Al Jazeera analyzed how Tehran views Trump's decision to sideline Vice President Vance from talks. Iran continues to demand seven conditions with clear sequencing. Fox News reported that Trump said on Truth Social that the US no longer needs a nuclear deal. [[TAG:info:no-deal posture]]

sections.title: Asia-Pacific
sections.summary: ASEAN opens in Manila with South China Sea code set to miss deadline; Manila, Canberra upgrade pact

paragraphs.heading: ASEAN Summit
paragraphs.body: The Philippine Star and AP, via ABC News, reported that the 49th ASEAN summit opened in Manila, with global conflicts and their impact at the top of the agenda. President Marcos opened the plenary without giving a timeline for the South China Sea code of conduct, which ASEAN had targeted for 2026. A diplomat told AFP that no code is expected to be signed at the summit. [[TAG:warning:code delayed]]

paragraphs.heading: Defense Upgrade
paragraphs.body: Anadolu and the Japan Times reported that the Philippines and Australia signed an upgraded defense cooperation arrangement in Manila, witnessed by Prime Minister Anthony Albanese. It covers joint exercises, procurement and disaster response. Philippine Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro said it bolsters a credible deterrent posture. Bloomberg framed it as a response to China. [[TAG:info:deterrence]]

sections.title: Europe and Ukraine
sections.summary: France's fifth Saturday of protests draws about 106,000; Ukraine prepares the war's largest swap

paragraphs.heading: France
paragraphs.body: Al Jazeera and France 24 reported that the interior ministry counted about 106,000 protesters nationwide on Saturday, down from 146,000 a week earlier, while student unions claimed far more. It was the fifth straight Saturday of protests over living costs, public services and police violence. Tear gas was used in Paris, Nantes and Bordeaux, and Paris prosecutors reported 45 arrests in the capital. Riviera Radio said about 70,000 police were deployed. [[TAG:warning:unrest continues]]

paragraphs.heading: Ukraine
paragraphs.body: RBC-Ukraine reported that the Trump team has begun preparations for the largest-ever Ukraine-Russia prisoner exchange, and that Zelensky rejected a Russian proposal for a humanitarian mission in Kostiantynivka as a 'primitive move.' The Kyiv Independent reported Russian strikes on Zaporizhzhia that injured 50 people, including children, and a Ukrainian drone attack on Russia's largest oil refinery. [[TAG:danger:strikes continue]]

sections.title: Israel: The UTJ Track
sections.summary: UTJ leads Haredi contacts with Eisenkot's bloc while Shas stays close to Netanyahu

paragraphs.heading: Talks
paragraphs.body: The Times of Israel reported that Eisenkot and Liberman agreed to open talks with the Haredi parties, eyeing concessions on the military draft law. Yahoo News, quoting a former Shas spokesperson, reported that United Torah Judaism is leading the contacts because of Shas's deep ties to Likud. The Jerusalem Post said Netanyahu has told the Haredi parties they cannot trust Eisenkot's promises. [[TAG:info:draft concessions]]

paragraphs.heading: Netanyahu's Bind
paragraphs.body: A Jerusalem Post analysis said Netanyahu is buying time as the Haredi parties weigh an Eisenkot coalition, but lacks an alternative path of his own. Shas has called reports that it will join an Eisenkot government 'fake news.' [[TAG:warning:Shas holds out]]

sections.title: Pope in the Andes
sections.summary: Leo urges an end to violence in a remote Andes town; Peru names itself 'Land of Pope Leo XIV'

paragraphs.heading: Andes Mass
paragraphs.body: Al Jazeera reported that Pope Leo XIV urged an end to violence in Peru during a Mass in the remote Andes town of Santa Cruz de Succhabamba, which he reached by military helicopter. EWTN said he praised the evangelists of the Andes. Vatican News said he travels on Sunday to Cusco, the former Inca capital that John Paul II visited 41 years ago, where Leo will meet representatives of popular devotion at Saqsaywaman. [[TAG:info:Cusco Sunday]]

paragraphs.heading: Decree
paragraphs.body: Latin Times reported that Peru's government published a decree naming the country the 'Land of Pope Leo XIV.' [[TAG:success:national honor]]
